The operators define a constrained optimization problem where free-tier models are preferred over paid twins based on cost inelasticity. The system enforces a dual logic: (1) functional equivalence between free and paid models, and (2) exclusion of redundant paid models from fallbacks. This is modeled as a Bayesian decision tree with cost-weighted branches. The failure mode occurs when paid models offer unique features not present in free versions, leading to suboptimal selection. The system assumes all models are deterministic within their respective tiers, which may break down under dynamic performance shifts. Dualities emerge in that the same model can be priced differently depending on tier, yet functionally equivalent. The epistemic trace reveals a preference for minimal-cost solutions under bounded rationality constraints.
